According to the World Health Organization, social distancing can help lower the pace and extent of spread of COVID-19 [2]. By maintaining a distance, we can reduce the virus transmission [2]. The goal of social distancing is to slow down the outbreak to reduce the chance of infection among high-risk populations and to reduce the burden on our health care system and workers [4]. Experts estimate that social distancing can help "flatten the curve" – successful social distancing can prevent surges in illness that could overwhelm our health care systems [3]. Social distancing can include large-scale measures like closing schools and bars, as well as individual decisions such as avoiding crowds and minimizing non-essential travel [4]. Many States have taken measures such as declaring holidays for schools, colleges, shutting down malls, theatres and even postponing sporting events to reduce chances of infection [0]. However, some studies suggest that the virus spreads beyond the recommended distancing parameters [8]. The concept of airborne transmission has been largely understated, and the World Health Organization acknowledged that aerosols can remain suspended in the air for longer durations in closed spaces [8]. Despite the limitations of social distancing, it is still considered an effective measure to reduce the transmission of COVID-19, and it is recommended by health officials to practice social distancing to prevent the spread of the virus [1]. However, it is also important to note that social distancing has socioeconomic and psychological repercussions, such as reduced human interaction, which has exacerbated mental health issues [8]. A more holistic approach that balances prevention with societal needs could better address the challenges posed by COVID-19 [8]. This approach may include enhanced ventilation systems, widespread and accessible rapid testing, coupled with strategic vaccination efforts [8]. In conclusion, while social distancing has its limitations, it is still considered an effective measure to reduce the transmission of COVID-19 [0, 1, 2, 3, 4].
